# What is NAP in Local SEO?

## What's NAP (and why should you care)?

In local SEO, NAP stands for name, address, and phone number. When a website URL is included, it's referred to as NAP+W.

Your NAP appears in [local business listings](https://moz.com/learn/seo/local-business-listing-components) and citations online, whether you manage them or not. It is included everywhere, from your website to your [Google Business Profile](https://moz.com/blog/beginners-guide-to-google-business-profile) and social profiles to business directories or citations on blogs or news websites. Each listing sends signals to Google about your business's legitimacy and location. Google values accurate information so its users, and your potential customers, have the best possible experience.

## Your business NAP is simply your Name, Address and Phone Number

Here is an example of NAP showing up online for a small bakery based on Colorado. The image shows a business name, complete address and phoine number with these details highlighted in orange, as you might see it on a directory or listings page. You might also have a similar fomat on your own website on the contact page. 

![](https://moz.com/images/learn/local/LC-What-is-NAP.png?auto=compress%2Cformat&fit=crop&dm=1737632915&s=8a380772d94fd3b722cc123b5f468421)

## Accuracy and consistency of your local NAP

The accuracy of your NAP across business listings is essential for local SEO success. When search engines encounter inconsistencies in this information, they may interpret them as separate businesses, potentially diluting your local search visibility. Additionally, Google itself has stated that it uses directories and listings to measure [prominence](https://support.google.com/business/answer/7091?hl=en#zippy=%2Crelevance%2Cdistance%2Cprominence), a key factor in its local algorithm. Maintaining accurate and consistent NAP information ensures that all your listings and citations work together to strengthen your local search rankings.

### Does NAP consistency matter?

Accuracy is more critically important than consistency these days. Google (and humans) understand, for the most part, that 'St' and 'Street' are the same or '5th' and 'Fifth' are the same. Accuracy is the key, and consistency is important, but use your common sense—it's okay if the formatting is a bit different as long as the information is correct.

This is, in part, because directories and aggregators all process and publish info differently. Some spell everything out; some accept what you input exactly, and some abbreviate. And some don't even show line 2 of the address.

## The benefits of NAP accuracy

When your NAP is correct and consistent, more local customers can find and contact your business. Alternatively, your customers could locate the wrong information and have a bad experience that they can share with friends, family, and online. In fact, in a [consumer survey](https://moz.com/local-business-review-survey-report), we found that 52% of people will leave a negative review after finding false or incorrect online information on assets like local business listings.

## Check NAP placement in these key places

Your NAP placement, accuracy and consistency isn't just about keeping Google happy—it's about making sure your customers can find you. Get it right, and you'll set yourself up for local SEO success. Make sure youhave your NAP listed correctly on your GBP, your website header, footer, and contact page, your social platforms and major local directories. 

### Tips for managing your NAP across the web

We know that managing your business information online is just another one of those jobs that keeps getting pushed down the list of priorities. Start with this simple workflow that will take under an hour to start reviewing and manaing tour NAP online: 

*   **Website fundamentals**: Your NAP needs to be complete and accurate on your site — in text format, not stored in images. Make sure it's listed in key areas that customers can check easily, like your header, footer, and contact page. If you have multiple locations create dedicated pages for each location.
*   **Google Business Profile**: Claim, optimize and manage your GBP listing. 
*   **Audit like a pro**: Use Google search operators to hunt down inconsistent listings.
*   **Directory domination**: Systematically correct your information across key business directories.
*   **Future-proof your NAP**: Keep a list of all your citations for quick updates when needed.

You can also streamline this process using [listing management software](https://moz.com/products/local). These platforms help to update and maintain your local listings across multiple directories from a single login.

## Inaccurate listings are costing you customers

**Moz Local ensures your information is consistent everywhere**

[Check my listing](https://moz.com/products/local/check-listing)

You're not alone if you've run into NAP headaches. # What is NAP and why is NAP consistency important?

Last updated: October 2025

[

![Stephanie Newton](https://brightlocal-corp-assets.s3.amazonaws.com/brightlocal-corp-2026/wp/uploads/2019/10/Steph.png)

Stephanie Newton

Guest Contributor



](https://www.brightlocal.com/author/stephanienewton/)

![What Is Nap Hub Header](https://brightlocal-corp-assets.s3.amazonaws.com/brightlocal-corp-2026/wp/uploads/2022/06/What-is-NAP-Hub-Header.png)

Three letters may not cast much of a shadow, but NAP is more critical than its stature may have you believe. This acronym is vital to local search success and can impact the online visibility of any local business. 

## **What does NAP stand for?** 

NAP is shorthand for three powerful pieces of local business information commonly found in directory listings, review sites, and other business profiles: 

*   Name
*   Address
*   Phone number 

Each element of the NAP trio conveys a vital chunk of information to a local consumer, making it easier for them to contact or visit you. If any one of the three foundational elements is missing from a business mention, it’s known to be a partial NAP. 

## Your Local Citations and NAP Data

As NAP data is commonly shared as part of any online mention of your business, you might find many of these citations you haven’t purposefully created yourself. 

Have you received coverage in a local newspaper article or presented at an industry expo? Have you hosted a local event or sponsored a local community sports team? These are examples of where a NAP citation may have been created without you realizing it.

Having others do some of the heavy lifting by creating NAP listings on your behalf can be both a blessing and a curse. The more of these citations you have, the bigger the SEO benefit you can expect to receive, and the more visible your business becomes to local consumers. 

However, that’s only the case if your business name, address, and phone number are accurate in each of the listings.

It’s quick and easy to create inaccuracies but time-consuming to fix them. For example, a local reporter might get your zip code wrong in their write-up about your latest award. Likewise, that industry seminar you’re speaking at may inadvertently share an outdated phone number or old address. 

Each time one piece of information differs, confusion and uncertainty are created. This can erode trust, leave consumers unable to contact you, and cause Google to place less trust in your business.

## **How do you make a NAP citation?** 

Any time your business name, address, and phone number are mentioned online, a NAP citation is created. This means there are a few different options for building your pool of listings:

*   Claiming your business profile on review platforms 
*   Adding your business to directory sites
*   Creating social media profiles with all profile information filled out
*   Creating events listings 
*   Local media mentions
*   Putting out press releases 
*   Through local business organizations, such as Chambers of Commerce
*   Exhibition listings 
*   Industry award nominations 
*   By authoring guest blog posts

![Nap Pr Example](https://brightlocal-corp-assets.s3.amazonaws.com/brightlocal-corp-2026/wp/uploads/2022/06/NAP-PR-example-640x347.png) ![Nap Directory Example](https://brightlocal-corp-assets.s3.amazonaws.com/brightlocal-corp-2026/wp/uploads/2022/06/NAP-Directory-Example-640x495.png) ![Facebook Nap Example](https://brightlocal-corp-assets.s3.amazonaws.com/brightlocal-corp-2026/wp/uploads/2022/06/Facebook-NAP-example-329x544.png)

Another way to build local citations is via your business website. The content on your site should naturally include your organization’s name, address, and phone number on various pages.
